nonvacuity: Closed witness on 512 outcomes. Every Bernoulli witness mass is positive and their sum is 1. Exact enumeration confirms all nonempty conditioning events, including probabilities 7/8, 87/128, 3825/4096 and 609/1024. No empty arm is used outside an explicit domain condition.

Take p=1/2, G=2, C=1, n_g=2, k_g=1, and y_i(z)=the treatment of the other unit. Both Bernoulli arms have positive own-assignment probabilities, and both fixed-count arms have size 1 on support. The two possible first-stage sets are nonempty. scratch/Check.lean compiles the basic positive-size/count conditions and a genuine two-unit uniform design.

The stated six-group, three-unit model has 20 first-stage sets and 3^6 assignments of positive mass per set, hence 14580 supported outcomes for each m=1,2. Every selected group has both arms present. Exact selected-group marginal enumeration confirms all retained local and six-group moments; integrating out auxiliary unselected draws leaves the canonical estimator law.

For the proper-domain theorem take G=3,C=2,n_g=4,m_g=2, so first-stage selection varies and each arm has 2 units. This parameter instance compiles in scratch/Check.lean. Schedules a_gi=i+1,b_gi=i have constant effects; a_gi=2i,b_gi=i give nonconstant effects and strictly positive bias. For the singleton claims take G=6,C=3,n_g=3,m=1 or 2 and baseline (1,2,3); both support sets exist and the strict-negativity premise is satisfiable.

Closed two-unit edge witness with four assignments of mass 1/4. The all-treated, complement and all-control event probabilities are respectively 1/4,3/4,1/4. All HT denominators are positive. Exact rational enumeration checks both schedules and both event choices.

The two-unit edge with the uniform design has positive extreme-event probabilities 1/4 at both units. Its nonconstant linear outcome 1+z_0+z_1 satisfies both extreme-event stability hypotheses. These design, positivity and stability conditions compile in scratch/Check.lean. The threshold outcome 1+2*I(z_0=z_1=true) also satisfies the stronger complement-event constancy assumption. A one-point finite design with E universal separately instantiates the general event identity.

The fixed symmetric, zero-diagonal four-unit single-edge matrix is a genuine network. There are 64 upper triangles, of which exact enumeration finds 32 asymmetric faulty outputs. Taking q=1/2 gives a genuine nondegenerate deletion draw. All list-index claims concern valid in-range indices; their defaults supply no asserted matrix entry.

For deletion counts d=0,1,2 there are 1,20,190 masks and 10 treated-unit choices each: 2110 positive-mass cases. Exact rational enumeration confirms every measured degree lies in [1,6], both observed control-exposure cells are nonempty, and both Hajek denominators are strictly positive in every case.

For the HT formulas one may take n=2, S=T equal to the single edge, and the uniform assignment design; measured d00 and d01 each have probability 1/4 at each unit. The subgraph and positivity premises compile in scratch/Check.lean. Genuine missing-edge instances are also supplied by the ten-unit graph with one deleted edge and a uniformly treated unit, where the degree bounds guarantee both event probabilities. Symmetric binary A and a zero-diagonal U equal to its upper triangle instantiate the matrix premises.

Closed four-path witness with independent cluster treatment probability 1/2. After first center 0, repeated draws of center 0 have geometric ratio 1/4; the eventual choices 1,2,3 each have conditional probability 1/3. Thus the trace series converge, without using the unsummable-tsum default. The five coded terminal masses sum to 1; the three repaired masses also sum to 1. An exact absorbing-chain calculation verifies both center laws and treatment supports.

Take n=2 and the empty-edge SimpleGraph. The admissible sequence [0,1] marks one new vertex at each step, completes after 2 steps, and its distinct centers have distance infinity. The positive-size graph instance compiles in scratch/Check.lean. Disconnected distance is Mathlib edist, so it does not collapse to zero.

Closed ten-cycle witness with 45 treatment pairs, each of mass 1/45; 10 are adjacent and 35 are not. Own-treatment probability is 1/5, and all four exposure probabilities are positive. Exact enumeration checks both expressions on every pair and all retained expectations.

Take the two-unit edge and the uniform design, with all four assignments of mass 1/4. Each own-treatment probability is 1/2 and each exposure probability is 1/4; the positive-design checks compile in scratch/Check.lean. The supplied cancellation schedule satisfies both unequal-outcome premises. Taking instead y_i11=2,y_i10=1 satisfies the positive-spillover premise and its strictness criterion, showing that branch is also nonvacuous.

The explicit assignment treating the first 50 units in groups 0,1,2 and first 25 in groups 3,4,5 has the required counts and positive fixed-count mass. There are 20 first-stage sets. Exact enumeration gives 8 with subclass counts (0,3) and 12 with (2,1); actual witness arm counts are 50/25. Undefined printed ratios are represented by Option.none rather than real division by zero.

Each of the 20 allowed first-stage sets has support: treat the first 50 units of each selected group and first 25 of each other group. The finite product fixed-count law is normalized, and both arms are positive in every group. In the all-high counterfactual law the own-arm probabilities are 2/3 and 1/3, so the target conditional means are ordinary conditional means. Exact first-stage enumeration gives weights 2/5 and 3/5, direct expectation 4/5 and bias -3/40. Generic pooling can be instantiated by a=2,b=1,A=9/2,B=2, and its empty-subclass boundary by a=A=0,b=3.

Closed printed-network witness with 45 uniformly sampled pairs. Every unit has strictly positive probability for each exposure; the degree range 3 through 6 prevents truncated natural subtraction from changing the formulas. The restricted supports have 20 and 19 members. Exact enumeration confirms the empty-cell assignment, all HT values and all three contrast means.
